title: Haimovitch Barred From Racing

page_data.en:
THE SHANGHAI TIMES, MONDAY, MAY 12, 1930.
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
I. D. REGISTER
No. 9087
19..5..30

HAIMOVITCH BARRED
FROM RACING
Race-Club Stewards Suspend Jockey Until
End Of Year

As the result of a meeting of
the Stewards of the Shanghai
Race Club on Saturday night, it
was decided to suspend Mr. Victor
Haimovitch from riding until
December 31, 1930. The decision
was reached following a special
meeting of the Stewards, at which
evidence was given by both Mr.
Haimovitch and Dr. E. J. Edgar
regarding the incident which led
to the suspension of Mr. Hai-
movitch from riding in the Cham-
pions on Wednesday last.
It will be recalled that Mr. Hai-
movitch, who has been riding ponies
successfully in Shanghai during
the past ten years, and who was
expected to ride Busy Bee in the
Champions, was not permitted at
the last minute to ride any pony
in the main event of the Spring
meeting. His mount, Busy Bee,
much to the surprise of the public,
was given to Mr. Bowling, who
successfully rode the pony to
victory.
It subsequently transpired that
Mr. Haimovitch had been debarred
from riding owing to certain char-
ges levelled against him by Dr.
Edgar in whose name the winning
ticket was held. Prior to the race,
the Stewards held a meeting and
suspended Mr. Haimovitch from
riding in the Champions.
On Saturday, a further inquiry
was held, as the result of which
Mr. Haimovitch was suspended
until the end of the current year.

（批：4/10 Special Branch
Information
12/5/30）

《字林西报》，1930年5月12日，星期一。
上海公共租界工部局警务处
身份登记册
第 9087 号
19..5..30

海伊莫维奇被禁止参加赛马
赛马会董事暂停其骑师资格至年底

由于上海赛马会董事于周六晚间举行会议，决定暂停维克多·海伊莫维奇（Victor Haimovitch）先生的骑乘资格，直至1930年12月31日。该决定是在董事特别会议后作出的，会上海伊莫维奇先生和 E. J. Edgar 博士均就导致海伊莫维奇先生在上周三“冠军赛”（Champions）中被停赛的事件提供了证词。
回顾可知，海伊莫维奇先生在过去十年中在上海成功策骑小型马（ponies），原定于在“冠军赛”中策骑“Busy Bee”，但在春季赛马会主要赛事的最后一刻，他被禁止策骑任何小型马。令公众大为惊讶的是，他的坐骑“Busy Bee”改由鲍林（Bowling）先生策骑，后者成功驾驭该马匹取得胜利。
随后事实表明，海伊莫维奇先生之所以被禁止参赛，是因为持有中奖彩票的 Edgar 博士对他提出了某些指控。赛前，董事们举行会议，暂停了海伊莫维奇先生在“冠军赛”中的骑乘资格。
周六，当局进行了进一步调查，结果是将海伊莫维奇先生暂停资格至本年度结束。

（批注：4/10 特别处
情报

S. SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. I. D. REGISTRY
No. 40, 9085
THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, MAY 8, 1930.
32 F 30

THE CHAMPIONS SENSATION

Jockey Designated to Ride Busy Bee Suspended by Stewards at Last Moment Following Statement by Ticket Holder

MR. V. HAIMOVITCH'S VERSION LAST NIGHT
Stewards' Finding of "Improper Suggestions" Said to be Due to Misunderstanding

The Champions Race yesterday afternoon was marked by a sensation which we believe to be unprecedented in the history of racing in Shanghai. While all the facts have not yet been made public, we understand that as a result of a complaint made to the Stewards of the Race Club, by the holder of a ticket on Busy Bee, the favourite in the race, the stewards held an investigation as a result of which Mr. V. Haimovitch, a most successful jockey, was indefinitely suspended, and Busy Bee, his mount, entrusted to another jockey. We understand that the decision of the Stewards, taken yesterday before the race, is open to further review, but, in view of the action taken and its general importance to racing in Shanghai, we are publishing the following though, naturally, under the greatest possible reserve.

In a criticism of the training gallops prior to the recent Hong-kong race meeting the sporting correspondent of one of the leading southern papers, whose pronouncements compel consideration, referred to Mr. Victor Haimovitch as "the best jockey in China." There is every reason for technical argument as to whether Haimovitch has hands, judgment of pace, knowledge of "horse" and all the other qualifications which go to make the perfect horseman and jockey, but there cannot be any possible denial of the fact that he is the finest winning jockey in China of the moment, and the finest there has been for many years, excelled possibly in this particular only by Mr. Frank Vida, who was an acknowledged horseman as well.

The Notice of Suspension
In the circumstances, there was naturally a sensation when, prior to the race for the Shanghai Champions yesterday—the most important race on any course in the Far East, and in which Mr. Haimovitch was engaged to ride one of the greatest possible racing certainties for many years—it was announced that he had been suspended indefinitely from riding. The announcement was made in a notification published on the Shanghai Race Club's notice boards, and so available only to members, but, in view of its importance, it seems only proper to make it generally known. The announcement was:—

The Stewards after hearing evidence on a report made in connection with Mr. V. Haimovitch and the drawer of "Busy Bee" in the "A" Sweep, are unanimously of the opinion that improper suggestions were made and have suspended Mr. Haimovitch indefinitely.
By order of the Stewards,
A. W. OLSEN.
Secretary, Shanghai Race Club.

As a consequence of the above, Mr. Haimovitch, who would have ridden Busy Bee, gave the mount to Mr. W. Bowling, who had been engaged to ride the stable's second string, Banquet Eve, the latter being taken over by Mr. A. F. Clarke, and the stable's third string (Election Eve), being ridden by Mr. T. J. Rothe. Busy Bee won very easily in time equalling record, and Banquet Eve was fourth.

Mr. Haimovitch's Statement
We are informed by Mr. Haimovitch that his suspension was due to a complete misunderstanding by Dr. Edgar of certain remarks passed immediately before the "Champions". He was in the dressing room, he informs us, when he heard that Dr. Edgar had drawn Busy Bee in the sweep. An offer to buy a one-tenth interest in the horse made by Mr. Haimovitch, and certain allusions to the respective chances of Busy Bee and Banquet Eve, were apparently taken as meaning that a share in the ticket would be an incentive to win.
The word "cinch" regarding the chances of Busy Bee figured largely in the alleged misunderstanding. This was said to have been heard as "switch." A statement by Mr. Haimovitch that Banquet Eve was "dangerous" also featured in the complaint to the stewards.
Mr. Haimovitch was confident that the stewards would on closer consideration of the whole matter, take steps to rectify an injustice. He had been a leading jockey for many years and his integrity had never previously been questioned. He informed us that he was out to make a record in the race, and that his offer to buy a one-tenth share in Dr. Edgar's ticket, which was not against the rules, was made in good faith and in a sporting spirit.

(Special Branch
Information 6/5/30)

S. 上海公共租界工部局警务处
C. I. D. 登记处
第 40, 9085 号
《字林西报》，1930年5月8日，星期四。
32 F 30

“冠军赛”轰动事件

因持票人发表声明，原定策骑“Busy Bee”的骑师在最后时刻被董事停职

V. 海伊莫维奇先生昨晚的说法
称董事认定存在“不当暗示”系出于误解

昨日下午的“冠军赛”出现了一起我们认为在上海赛马史上前所未有的轰动事件。虽然所有事实尚未公之于众，但我们获悉，由于“Busy Bee”（该赛事的热门马匹）的一名彩票持有人向赛马会董事提出投诉，董事们随即展开调查，结果是最为成功的骑师之一 V. 海伊莫维奇先生被无限期停职，而其坐骑“Busy Bee”则转交另一名骑师策骑。我们了解到，董事们于赛前昨日作出的这一决定仍有待进一步复议，但鉴于已采取的行动及其对上海赛马界的普遍重要性，我们在此尽可能谨慎地发布以下内容。

在评论近期香港赛马会之前的训练慢跑时，某家主要南方报纸的体育记者——其言论值得重视——称维克多·海伊莫维奇先生为“中国最佳骑师”。关于海伊莫维奇是否具备手感、配速判断力、对“马匹”的了解以及构成完美马术师和骑师的所有其他素质，技术上虽有争论余地，但不可否认的事实是，他是目前中国最出色的获胜骑师，也是多年来最优秀的一位，或许只有同样被公认的马术师弗兰克·维达（Frank Vida）先生在这一方面能胜过他。

停职通知
在这种情况下，当昨日上海“冠军赛”——远东任何赛马场上最重要的比赛，且海伊莫维奇先生受聘策骑一匹多年来最具胜算的马匹——赛前宣布他被无限期停止骑乘资格时，自然引起了轰动。该公告刊登在上海赛马会的布告栏上，因此仅会员可见，但鉴于其重要性，似乎理应让公众知晓。公告如下：—

董事们在听取了关于 V. 海伊莫维奇先生与“A”组彩券中“Busy Bee”抽签人的相关报告证据后，一致意见认为存在不当暗示，并据此无限期暂停海伊莫维奇先生的资格。
奉董事命令，
A. W. OLSEN.
上海赛马会秘书。

因此，原应策骑“Busy Bee”的海伊莫维奇先生将坐骑让给了 W. Bowling 先生，后者原本受聘策骑马房的第二主力“Banquet Eve”，而“Banquet Eve”则改由 A. F. Clarke 先生策骑，马房的第三主力（“Election Eve”）由 T. J. Rothe 先生策骑。“Busy Bee”轻松获胜，时间平了纪录，“Banquet Eve”获得第四名。

海伊莫维奇先生的声明
据海伊莫维奇先生告知，他的停职是由于 Edgar 博士完全误解了在“冠军赛”前夕所说的某些话语。他告诉我们，当时他在更衣室，听说 Edgar 博士在彩券抽签中抽中了“Busy Bee”。海伊莫维奇先生提出购买该马匹十分之一权益的提议，以及对“Busy Bee”和“Banquet Eve”各自胜算的某些提及，显然被理解为分享彩票权益将成为获胜的动机。
关于“Busy Bee”胜算的“稳赢”（cinch）一词在很大程度上构成了所谓的误解。据说这个词被听成了“调换”（switch）。海伊莫维奇先生称“Banquet Eve”具有“危险性”的陈述也出现在向董事提出的投诉中。
海伊莫维奇先生相信，董事们在更仔细地考虑整个事件后，将采取措施纠正这一不公。他多年来一直是顶尖骑师，其正直品行此前从未受到质疑。他告诉我们，他旨在比赛中创造纪录，而他提出购买 Edgar 博士彩票十分之一份额的提议并不违反规则，是出于诚意和体育精神作出的。

（特别处
情报 1930年5月6日）

(C.I.D.) Office Notes
D.C.J.
No.
File No. C085
April 20, 1928.

There is nothing on record concerning
V. Haimovitch.
Victor M. Haimovitch is a popular
member of the British-Jewish community
of Shanghai and a member of the
Shanghai Brokers Association, his
office being at 20 Museum Road. He
is also a well-known jockey and rider
for Mr. H.S. Elias and prominent
Chinese owners at most of the local
race meetings where his methods of
riding have been frequently severely
criticised by the public. His morals
also leave much to be desired.
Haimovitch, who is popularly known
as "Vick" was put up for the Shanghai
Race Club but was black balled
at a meeting held in the Club's
premises on April 16, owing it is
said to his having been connected
with Mr Judah Ezra in the
"Baseball Scandal" in Shanghai in
August 1918. This latter incident
was the cause of a great deal of
talk in town and resulted in
Mr Judah Ezra's name being re-
moved from the rolls of members
of the Shanghai Race Club.
Several articles referring to the
Baseball Scandal are to be found
in the North China Herald of
August 24 and 31 and September 14,
1918 respectively.

Jn. Hamb
Wm. A. Robertson
D.I.

(C.I.D.) 办公室笔记
D.C.J.
编号
档案号 C085
1928年4月20日。

关于 V. 海伊莫维奇，记录中没有任何内容。
维克多·M. 海伊莫维奇是上海英籍犹太人社群中受欢迎的成员，也是上海经纪人协会的成员，其办公室位于博物馆路20号。他还是一位知名的骑师，为 H.S. Elias 先生及多位显赫的中国马主在大多数本地赛马会上策骑，但其骑乘方法经常受到公众的严厉批评。他的道德品行也大有欠缺。
海伊莫维奇，俗称“维克”（Vick），曾被提名为上海赛马会会员，但在4月16日于会所举行的会议上被黑球否决（black balled），据称是因为他在1918年8月上海的“棒球丑闻”中与 Judah Ezra 先生有牵连。后一事件在当时引起了大量议论，并导致 Judah Ezra 先生的名字从上海赛马会会员名册中除名。
关于棒球丑闻的几篇文章分别见于1918年8月24日、31日和9月14日的《北华捷报》。

Jn. Hamb
Wm. A. Robertson
侦探督察
